title: When the Escarpment Turns
premise: Tamsin Marchetti, a railroad engineer who has spent a decade outrunning the fallout of a bridge collapse he didn't cause, is hired to survey closed mountain lines above the Kessarin River. When an upriver expedition goes silent, he's conscripted by its desperate backer to reach them — and discovers the expedition found the wreck of the Corvane, a salvage fleet's long-buried secret carrying proof of who really caused the collapse. Racing the fleet through six tides of narrowing gorges before the monsoon seals the river, Tamsin must choose between the loyalty of the crew that becomes his family and the truth that will finally let him stop running. He reaches the wreck on the sixth tide, exposes the salvage magnate's forgery at the cost of the line itself, and chooses to stay — building something permanent with the people who stayed for him.
about_author: Kestrel Lockridge is the pen name of a former field surveyor who spent eight years mapping decommissioned rail corridors across three continents before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who measure the world precisely and still fail to measure themselves.

chapters.title: The Last Timetable
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In a rain-soaked junction town, Tamsin takes a survey contract for closed mountain lines, hiding his real name and his past behind a forged credential. The emotional beat is restless caution: he's learned that every job is temporary, every attachment a liability.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. His employer, the imperious salvage heiress Odile Vantrease, reveals the expedition she funded upriver has gone silent for nine days, and the monsoon arrives in six tides. She offers triple pay and a threat. The beat is entrapment: Tamsin recognizes the trap but can't refuse it.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, introducing the boat crew: gruff pilot Brannoc, superstitious deckhand Sefa, and Odile's brittle nephew Callum. First night on the Kessarin, small frictions and small kindnesses. The beat is reluctant belonging beginning despite himself.

chapters.title: Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Surveying an abandoned cliffside tunnel, he finds fresh blasting charges — someone is sealing the route ahead of them. Sabotage, not accident. The beat is dread sharpening into purpose: this silence was manufactured.

chapters.title: What Sefa Knows
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. She reads the river's moods and warns that the water is being held upstream — a weir, illegally. Tamsin realizes the salvage fleet controls the tides themselves. The beat is awe and unease: nature itself has been weaponized against them.

chapters.title: The Magnate's Shadow
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A black-hulled fleet tender overtakes them; aboard is Renn Halvard, the salvage magnate whose name Tamsin knows from the collapse inquiry years ago. Halvard offers to buy their turn-back. The beat is recognition: his past and this mission are the same story.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Bargain
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Flashback woven with present: Brannoc once ran cargo for Halvard and owes him a debt. He quietly signals the tender their heading. The beat is guilt — the first betrayal, done out of love for a daughter Halvard holds over him.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. They find the expedition's base camp: burned radio mast, abandoned gear, one survivor delirious with fever who whispers about 'the manifest.' The beat is horror curdling into resolve — the expedition was hunted, not lost.

chapters.title: The Fever Chart
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Nursing the survivor, Tamsin pieces together her fragments: the expedition found the Corvane wreck, and aboard it, documents proving the collapse Tamsin fled was engineered — by Halvard's company. The beat is vertigo: the map of his own ruin redrawn.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Weir
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile confronts Brannoc about the signal; Sefa defends him; the crew nearly fractures. Odile admits her expedition was never about salvage rights — it was about her father's partnership in the crime. The beat is raw honesty: everyone aboard is running from something.

chapters.title: Two Days of Water
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Halvard opens the weir gates early, flooding the gorge and destroying their moorings; they lose half their supplies riding the surge. The beat is survival fury — the race is no longer for profit or truth, but for breath.

chapters.title: The Portage
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The crew hauls the boat over a landslide on foot through leech-hung jungle, Callum collapsing and being carried. Small sacrifices knit them together. The beat is found family forged in exhaustion and shared weight.

chapters.title: Third Tide
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Halfway point. Tamsin confesses his true identity to the crew — the engineer blamed for the collapse, exiled by Halvard's forged report. The beat is vulnerability met not with rejection but with Brannoc's rough absolution: 'We all signed papers we didn't read.'

chapters.title: Halvard's Mercy
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Halvard captures Callum scouting ahead and releases him with an offer: deliver Tamsin, and everyone else walks free — including Brannoc's daughter. Callum returns saying nothing. The beat is corrosive temptation carried like a stone.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Bells
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A night run through a gorge where the fleet has strung warning wires and listening posts; Sefa navigates by sound alone. They pass, barely. The beat is triumphant tension — skill and trust beating money and machinery.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Brannoc learns Callum made a deal and intercepts him before he can act; instead of exposing him, Brannoc shares his own debt. The beat is grace between guilty men — loyalty chosen knowingly, not naively.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: The Wreck
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They reach the Corvane, half-swallowed by the riverbank, and dive as the monsoon's first outer bands hit. Inside: the sealed strongroom, the original manifests, and evidence of the engineered collapse. The beat is grim vindication in rising water.

chapters.title: The Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Halvard's ships seal the gorge; Odile trades herself as hostage to buy the crew time to move the documents. The beat is sacrifice reversing her arc — the woman who bought loyalty now spends herself for it.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Climax. With the monsoon breaking, Tamsin uses his engineer's knowledge to collapse the gorge's old viaduct across the channel, trapping the fleet and forcing Halvard to negotiate. Confrontation on the flooding deck: truth versus power, tide versus timetable. The beat is everything staked at once.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Aftermath of the confrontation: Halvard arrested when the documents reach the river authority, Odile wounded but alive, the Corvane claimed by the rising water forever. The beat is grief and release — some things are won only by letting them sink.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Downriver, Tamsin testifies under his own name for the first time in ten years, clearing the dead and convicting the living. The beat is quiet catharsis — the running stops, and standing still costs nothing he can't pay.

chapters.title: When the Escarpment Turns
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, epilogue. One year later: Tamsin engineering the rebuilding of the mountain line with Brannoc, Sefa, and Callum as crew, Odile funding it honestly. The escarpment turns gold at sunset. The beat is arrival — a man who kept moving finally builds something that stays.
